rationale: C05 plausibly supplied material language and argumentative structure for the later letter: both describe the Polish people suffering under Communist or foreign oppression, emphasize an irrepressible spiritual commitment to freedom, and predict that repression cannot extinguish that commitment. The child's phrase about the Polish nation's “inextinguishable love of freedom” closely echoes C05's statement that Poland's religious spirit “will never be subdued or extinguished.” C24 has a similar faith-and-freedom symbolism under totalitarian persecution, while C02 supplies the more generic formulation of a people confidently “meeting the test.”
